name: InfiniteTalk Video-to-Video (motion + lip-sync)
description: Audio-driven lip-sync applied on top of a driving motion clip. Loads a source video (e.g. a subject dancing/twirling from a t2v/i2v run), encodes its motion, and re-samples it to lip-sync a voice line while preserving the body motion (Wan 2.1 I2V backbone + InfiniteTalk/MultiTalk). Use this instead of infinitetalk_i2v when you want real body motion, not just a talking head.

prompt.description: Drives expression. The body motion comes from the driving video, so keep this simple.

video.description: Driving motion video filename (staged to ComfyUI input). Its motion is preserved; supplies the body movement.

audio.description: Input audio filename (wav) staged to ComfyUI input. Drives lip-sync + clip length.

negative_prompt.default: bright tones, overexposed, static, blurred details, subtitles, style, works, paintings, images, static, overall gray, worst quality, low quality, JPEG compression residue, ugly, incomplete, extra fingers, poorly drawn hands, poorly drawn faces, deformed, disfigured, misshapen limbs, fused fingers, still picture, messy background, three legs, many people in the background, walking backwards

denoise_strength.description: V2V motion-adherence knob — THE key dial. At 1.0 the driving video is noised to pure noise and InfiniteTalk regenerates a talking head from the first frame, DISCARDING the body motion (the subject won't bend/dance). Lower preserves the driving motion: the sampler starts the denoise partway and keeps the driving latents. 0.5 mirrors Kijai's V2V example (start denoise ~halfway) — keeps body motion while still re-animating the mouth. Go lower (0.3-0.4) to lock motion harder, higher (0.6-0.7) for stronger lip-sync at the cost of motion fidelity.

width.description: Resize target width (divisible by 16). Motion clips are usually landscape; 832x480 is the tuned default.

length.description: OUTPUT frame count (num_frames for the audio embeds) — NOT an input cap. The driving clip is now loaded in full (frame_load_cap=0) and windowed by frame_window_size(81), matching Kijai's reference. For v2v the API auto-derives this from the driving clip duration x fps when the caller leaves it None, so the motion+lip-sync cover the whole clip instead of being truncated. At 25fps: 81 frames ~= 3.2s. The endpoint caps auto-derived length at 201 (~8s) to bound RAM on 12GB nodes.

fps.description: InfiniteTalk is trained at 25fps. Also re-times the driving video to this rate (force_rate). Do not change unless you know why.

steps.description: Sampler steps. 4 matches Kijai's V2V reference (the lightx2v speed-distill LoRA is trained for ~4 steps). With denoise_strength 0.5 the sampler starts ~halfway (start_step 2 of 4), preserving driving motion.

blocks_to_swap.description: Block-swap count for low-VRAM. 12 is the proven sweet spot on a 12GB card with the Q3_K_S GGUF: ~10GB VRAM used, GPU at 95%, no OOM. Higher = less VRAM but GPU-starved/slow; lower risks OOM.

model.description: GGUF-quantized Wan2.1 I2V 14B backbone (~7.9GB). Fits 12GB card with block-swap. fp8 safetensors OOMs a 12GB card.

multitalk_model.description: GGUF-quantized InfiniteTalk module (~1.3GB). Must be GGUF to pair with the GGUF backbone.
